mentalMap.label: The problem
mentalMap.sub: agreement + validity + termination against Byzantine nodes; every mechanism spends something scarce

mentalMap.label: Proof of Work
mentalMap.sub: nonce → double SHA-256 → under target; 2016-block retarget; 51% = outspend, not outrun

mentalMap.label: Proof of Stake
mentalMap.sub: stake-weighted selection; slashing for equivocation; nothing-at-stake; 33%/66% thresholds

mentalMap.label: Proof of Burn
mentalMap.sub: send to an unspendable address; receipt is the proof; supply falls forever

mentalMap.label: Proof of Activity
mentalMap.sub: PoW mine → stake reward → confirm; not Proof of Authority

mentalMap.label: Proof of Elapsed Time
mentalMap.sub: random wait in a TEE, shortest wait wins; permissioned; trust the chip vendor

mentalMap.label: SBFT
mentalMap.sub: pre-prepare → prepare → commit → execute; 3f+1 nodes, 2f+1 quorum, deterministic finality

mentalMap.label: Mining
mentalMap.sub: double SHA-256 nonce sweep; subsidy 50/2^n every 210,000 blocks; then fees fund security

topExamQuestions: What is a consensus mechanism, what properties must it deliver, and what does each mechanism spend? (5 marks)
Explain Proof of Work with the target/difficulty rule, the nonce search, the 51% attack and the cost of attacking. (15 marks)
Explain Proof of Stake: selection by stake, slashing, nothing-at-stake and long-range attacks, deterministic finality. (15 marks)
Explain SBFT: the leader-based voting rounds, quorum sizes, the 3f+1 bound with a computation, and the finality guarantee. (15 marks)
What is Proof of Burn, what does a participant actually do, and why does it bootstrap a new chain? (5 marks)
Explain Proof of Activity as a PoW-plus-PoS hybrid and distinguish it from pure PoW, pure PoS and Proof of Authority. (5 marks)
Explain Proof of Elapsed Time and the trust assumption behind its TEE. (5 marks)
Explain mining: the double-SHA-256 nonce search, the subsidy halving schedule and the move to fee-funded security. (5 marks)
drill: Three properties of a consensus protocol?
Electricity and hardware — the target is the rule, difficulty is its inverse
How often is PoW difficulty retargeted?
What can a 51% attacker do and not do?
Double-spend and censor; cannot change tx contents or steal keys; must outspend the honest network
Provable double-signing of conflicting blocks — part of the stake is burned
Validator could back both forks for free; slashing is the fix
~33% to reorganise a weakly finalised chain, ~66% to break finality
PoB: what does the participant do?
Send tokens to a provably unspendable address — the receipt is the proof
PoA in this syllabus is what?
The PoW+PoS hybrid: mine, stake the reward, confirm by stake — NOT Proof of Authority
A TEE-signed certificate over a random wait; the shortest wait wins
SBFT node count for f faulty nodes?
SHA-256 applied twice to the 80-byte header, nonce varied until under target
